newsitem.title: USA: U.S. jury convicts blacks in New York murder.
newsitem.headline: U.S. jury convicts blacks in New York murder.

text.p: A federal jury on Monday found two black men guilty in the fatal stabbing of a Hasidic Jew in a widely watched case stemming from the 1991 racial violence in the Crown Heights section of Brooklyn.
At issue was whether the defendants were part of a racist vigilante mob that killed Yankel Rosenbaum or scapegoats for the Jewish student's murder on the first of four nights of rioting.
The violence marked one of the most serious outbreaks of unrest in New York City in many years.
The case charged Lemrick Nelson, 21, who was previously acquitted of the same murder in state court, with violating Rosenbaum's civil rights.
After his acquittal by the state court jury, many Hasidic Jews and elected officials demanded a federal investigation. That inquiry eventually led to the current trial.
A co-defendant, 43-year-old Charles Price, was charged with aiding and abetting the civil rights violation by inciting the crowd to seek revenge on Jews.
Both men were found guilty on Monday by a jury after four days of deliberations.

The murder of Rosenbaum, an Australian doctoral student, was sparked by an auto accident in which a Hasidic driver killed a seven-year-old boy. The accident took place in the Crown Heights section of Brooklyn where there is often friction between blacks and Hasidic Jews.
At the scene of the accident, a Jewish ambulance service was the first to arrive, and they removed the driver who was already being abused by a crowd that had formed quickly.
Defence lawyers argued that Nelson and Price did not commit the crimes.
"Lemrick Nelson was made the sacrificial lamb. The police framed him, set him up," Nelson's lawyer Christine Yaris said during closing arguments.

The most controversial evidence was a pair of faded, baggy blue jeans Nelson was allegedly wearing when he was arrested. Yaris asked Nelson to try on the pants in court, where they fell down around his knees.
"If they don't fit now, in this courtroom, they didn't fit then," Yaris said, reminding jurors that Nelson was taller and heavier now than he was five-and-a-half years ago.

Defence lawyers also argued that other inconsistencies and conflicting testimony, including alleged admissions Nelson made to the police, his former roommate and a former girlfriend, all prove that Nelson was set up.

Assistant U.S. Attorney Valerie Caproni argued that there was a common thread in all the testimony that proved Nelson was responsible for Rosenbaum's death, especially statements from his ex-girlfriend Travionne Shaw.
"Travionne Shaw's testimony fits like a glove," Caproni said. "Lemrick Nelson told her a story that only one other person in the world knew and Yankel Rosenbaum took it to his grave."
